drowning_deaths.short_description: Annual count of unintentional drowning deaths.
drowning_deaths.long_description: Annual count of deaths from unintentional drowning (ICD-10 underlying cause of death codes W65, W66, W67, W68, W69, W70, W73, W74), from CDC WONDER's Underlying Cause of Death database. Cells representing fewer than 10 deaths are suppressed by CDC; these are coded here as -999 with suppressed_flag = 1, meaning 'between 1 and 9 deaths', not 'no deaths'. A true zero is reported as 0.
drowning_deaths.statement: In {location}, there were {value} unintentional drowning deaths in {time}.

drowning_population.long_name: Population denominator used for the drowning crude rate
drowning_population.short_description: Population denominator for the drowning crude rate.
drowning_population.long_description: Bridged-race population estimate used by CDC WONDER as the denominator for the drowning crude rate, for the matching geography, year, and demographic group. CDC does not publish a denominator for every geography/demographic combination (notably county by age group, where it reports 'Not Applicable'); those cells are coded here as -999 with missing_denom_flag = 1.
drowning_population.statement: In {location}, the population denominator was {value} in {time}.

drowning_crude_rate.long_name: Unintentional drowning death rate per 100,000 population
drowning_crude_rate.short_description: Annual unintentional drowning death rate per 100,000 population.
drowning_crude_rate.long_description: Crude rate of unintentional drowning deaths per 100,000 population, as reported by CDC WONDER's Underlying Cause of Death database (ICD-10 codes W65, W66, W67, W68, W69, W70, W73, W74). Coded as -999 wherever no rate could be reported or computed -- because the underlying death count was suppressed for confidentiality (suppressed_flag = 1, fewer than 10 deaths) or because no population denominator exists for that geography and demographic combination (missing_denom_flag = 1). Both flags can be 1 on the same row.
drowning_crude_rate.statement: In {location}, the unintentional drowning death rate was {value} per 100,000 population in {time}.

drowning_crude_rate_lcl.long_name: Lower bound of the 95% confidence interval for the drowning crude rate
drowning_crude_rate_lcl.short_description: Lower 95% confidence bound for the drowning death rate.
drowning_crude_rate_lcl.long_description: Lower bound of the 95% confidence interval for drowning_crude_rate, as reported by CDC WONDER. Coded as -999 wherever no bound is available: either CDC did not publish one (flagged by suppressed_flag = 1 or missing_denom_flag = 1), or this is a derived row CDC never itself reports a CI for -- the 'Overall' (all-sexes) rows, computed here by summing sex-specific rows, and all county-level age rows, whose crude rate is derived from a population estimated here rather than reported by CDC (see drowning_population). Do not plot error bars wherever this is -999.
drowning_crude_rate_lcl.statement: In {location}, the lower bound of the 95% CI for the drowning death rate was {value} in {time}.

drowning_crude_rate_ucl.long_name: Upper bound of the 95% confidence interval for the drowning crude rate
drowning_crude_rate_ucl.short_description: Upper 95% confidence bound for the drowning death rate.
drowning_crude_rate_ucl.long_description: Upper bound of the 95% confidence interval for drowning_crude_rate, as reported by CDC WONDER. Coded as -999 wherever no bound is available: either CDC did not publish one (flagged by suppressed_flag = 1 or missing_denom_flag = 1), or this is a derived row CDC never itself reports a CI for -- the 'Overall' (all-sexes) rows, computed here by summing sex-specific rows, and all county-level age rows, whose crude rate is derived from a population estimated here rather than reported by CDC (see drowning_population). Do not plot error bars wherever this is -999.
drowning_crude_rate_ucl.statement: In {location}, the upper bound of the 95% CI for the drowning death rate was {value} in {time}.

cdc_wonder_ucd_drowning.name: CDC WONDER Underlying Cause of Death, 2018-2024 (ICD-10, expanded)
cdc_wonder_ucd_drowning.organization: CDC National Center for Health Statistics
cdc_wonder_ucd_drowning.description: Mortality data from death certificates filed in the 50 states and the District of Columbia, queried through CDC WONDER's Underlying Cause of Death (ICD-10, expanded) database and restricted to unintentional drowning: ICD-10 codes W65 (bathtub), W66 (swimming pool fall), W67 (in swimming pool), W68 (fall into swimming pool), W69 (natural water), W70 (fall into natural water), W73 (other specified drowning/submersion), and W74 (unspecified drowning/submersion). Data are broken out separately by age group, sex, single race, and Hispanic origin (each queried independently, not cross-tabulated), at both the state and county level, for years 2018-2024. State and county both use CDC WONDER's Ten-Year Age Groups (<1, 1-4, 5-14, 15-24, ..., 85+), but the two levels differ in how population is sourced. At the state level, CDC WONDER reports Population and Crude Rate directly for Ten-Year Age Groups. At the county level, CDC WONDER reports Deaths only for this age variable -- Population and Crude Rate remain checked (mandatory) in the query form but the server omits them from the export regardless, for every state and year. County-level population is therefore derived here by summing CDC's Five-Year Age Groups county population export into the same Ten-Year buckets (e.g. 5-9 + 10-14 = 5-14); crude_rate is then recomputed from that derived population rather than taken from CDC directly, so drowning_crude_rate_lcl/_ucl are not populated for county-level age rows (a valid confidence interval needs CDC's own interval method, which this derivation does not replicate). This also surfaces a further CDC limitation: county-level population is reported as 'Not Applicable' for the <1, 1-4, and 85+ Five-Year groups nationwide, for every county regardless of size -- so missing_denom_flag = 1 for those three Ten-Year buckets at the county level essentially always, and county-level drowning rates (though not death counts) are structurally unavailable for infants/toddlers and the oldest age group. Missing values are coded as -999, accompanied by two independent row-level indicator columns (a true zero is reported as 0, never -999). suppressed_flag = 1 where CDC withheld a cell for confidentiality (any cell representing fewer than 10 deaths); this affects the death count and the rates derived from it, never the population. missing_denom_flag = 1 where no population denominator exists for that geography and demographic combination (CDC reports 'Not Applicable' or 'Not Available', or -- for county-level age specifically -- the Five-Year population export used to derive it was itself missing); this affects the population and the rates derived from it, never the death count. The two are not mutually exclusive and are both 1 on rows carrying both markers, which is common at the county level. No national total is included: CDC WONDER does not provide one directly for this query design, and summing state totals that each contain suppressed cells of unknown magnitude would produce a biased estimate.
cdc_wonder_ucd_drowning.restrictions: Data Use Restrictions: The Public Health Service Act (42 U.S.C. 242m(d)) provides that the data collected by the National Center for Health Statistics (NCHS) may be used only for the purpose for which they were obtained; any effort to determine the identity of any reported cases, or to use the information for any purpose other than for health statistical reporting and analysis, is against the law. Therefore users will: (1) Use these data for health statistical reporting and analysis only. (2) Do not present or publish birth counts of 9 or fewer or birth rates based on counts of nine or fewer (in figures, graphs, maps, tables, etc.). (3) Make no attempt to learn the identity of any person or establishment included in these data. (4) Make no disclosure or other use of the identity of any person or establishment discovered inadvertently and advise the NCHS Confidentiality Officer of any such discovery: Confidentiality Officer, National Center for Health Statistics, 3311 Toledo Road, Hyattsville, MD 20782. Telephone 888-642-4159. Email: nchsconfidentiality@cdc.gov. Sanctions for Violating Rules: Researchers who violate the terms of the data use restrictions will lose access to WONDER and their sponsors and institutions will be notified. Researchers who are suspected of violating the rules may be prevented from using WONDER until an investigation can be completed. Deliberately making a false statement in any matter within the jurisdiction of any department or agency of the Federal government violates 18 USC 1001 and is punishable by a fine of up to $10,000 or up to 5 years in prison, or both..
